The gate module etch process has been shown to exhibit a strong correlation to the temperature profile of the electrostatic chuck (ESCs) used in the etch chamber.
the SensArray ESC temperature profile is strongly correlated to the gate recess and gate CD problems after gate etches.

the correlation between ESC temperature and gate CD and silicon recess after etch.
the correlation of ESC temperature profile and gate CD/CD-SEM measurement to investigate silicon recess after etch.
understanding the correlation between the ESC temperature and the silicon recess and gate CDs after etch.

a strong correlation between ESC temperature profile and silicon recess and gate CDs was observed.
a correlation between the ESC temperature profile and the gate CD/CD SEM measurement was observed.
the ESC temperature is the most important factor to control for a successful etch process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a correlation study was performed to investigate the impact of temperature on the silicon recess/gate CD after etch, and the correlation between the spatial temperature profile and the optical CD/CD-SEM measurements.

a correlation study between the temperature gradient across the wafer and the CD variation was done and it was found that the temperature gradient across wafer has a strong correlation with the CD variation.
we have shown a strong correlation between the spatial temperature profile and the silicon recess and gate line edge roughness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ESC temperature monitoring can be used to identify and correct etch related problems, such as silicon recess and gate critical dimension (CD).
a correlation between the temperature profile and CD variation can be established, thus enabling the use of the SensArray product as an ESC monitor to reduce the Si recess problem.
the ESC temperature profile is a very important factor for etching of the gate module.
